articles.summary: Jacob Rothman built a manufacturing business in China supplying major retailers
articles.body:
World Service , · 23 Sep 2026 , · 17 mins

Jacob Rothman moved from California to China and helped build a manufacturing business supplying some of the world's biggest retailers. We meet the co-founder of Velong Enterprises to hear how he built the company across Asia and how an unlikely career path took him to the heart of global manufacturing. articles.title: I Know Sun Damage Is Bad—but When Did It Become a Moral Failing?
articles.summary: Wear your sunscreen and mind your business.
articles.body:
Sun damage is often a target for cruel comments on social media, with skin-related remarks being made with full names and profile pictures, unlike comments about body shape or size.

Sun damage is a complex process influenced by genetics, lifestyle choices, and other factors, with discoloration often making a face appear older, not just wrinkles or creases.

Shame and humiliation are not effective strategies for encouraging sun protection, as they can lead to internalizing negative messages about appearance and aging.

It's a common talking point amongst millennials that younger generations wouldn't survive the anonymous brutality of the internet of yore. But as someone who was both there back then and is currently wedged deep in our modern social media age, I have to say—every day there is a TikTok comment that quite literally gives me pause with its staggering casual cruelty. The target is often a woman (of course), and the comment is almost always about her appearance, but there's a strange pattern you'll notice after a while. Leave a cutting remark about body shape or size, and you'll be brigaded (rightfully) with dozens of replies setting you straight. Skin, though? Particularly when it comes to signs of sun damage or the look of premature aging, there's no need to go anon—that "I'm bored, let's put on sunscreen" comment is made with a full name, profile picture, and a school tagged in their bio. The body positivity movement has made major strides in the past 20 years, but somewhere along the way, we left skin out of the equation. Sun damage is a particularly prime target, maybe because of the (much needed) mainstreaming of information around SPF and safe sun . There's a perceived culpability, a "you-did-this-to-yourself- yikes" undercurrent that seems to grant license to lob the meanest shit imaginable at unsuspecting posters, couched in smug morality. All sorts of lifestyle choices are apparent in our appearance—why does this one feel like such fair game?

The human brain has a remarkable ability to subconsciously track patterns and draw conclusions, critical for our survival (great for evading predators and now making sweeping inferences in DeuxMoi comment sections). Those mechanisms naturally extend to appearance—ourselves and others—but there's more cultural and social work at play than we realize. When it comes to evaluating sun damage, we seem to think we can read someone's values off their face. Has this person consciously chosen to skip sunscreen out of an inability to delay gratification? Are they not smart or well-read enough to know about its dangers? Are they a MAHA-adjacent SPF eschewer, convinced the chemical compounds are the real danger here? Each assumption turns a physical characteristic into a character assessment, collapsing the distance between what someone looks like and who we decide they must be. It's part of the problem with the whole "Republican makeup" accusation. The problem isn't recognizing that aesthetic trends can carry cultural associations, because they very much do. It's more the certainty with which we attempt to reverse-engineer character from traits that may be only partially chosen—or not chosen at all. And unlike excessive eyeliner, sun damage isn't something you can wash off at the end of the day.

The reality is, we don't always know what we're looking at. Sun damage is not just pigmentation or wrinkles, explains Dr. Shereene Idriss, board-certified dermatologist and founder of Idriss Dermatology in New York City . It's a complex process that manifests differently based on a number of factors, including genetics. "Some people age faster or appear more weathered because of genetics, despite taking proper precautions around sun exposure because aging is never one variable," she shares. Interestingly, Dr. Idriss also notes discoloration is oftentimes what makes a face read as older, rather than the stereotypical idea of wrinkles and creases—which is likely what spurs those nasty "you look 50" comments on a video of someone clearly sitting at a classroom desk wearing Brandy Melville. She also adds that not all brown spots, of any shade, automatically equal sun damage. She lists freckles and melasma as two examples—though UV exposure can exacerbate both of them, they're also influenced by genetics and hormones. Of course, her medical training and practice experience compel her to add in an important bottom line: While genetics are an undeniable factor in the look of aging, it's lifestyle choices that ultimately play a bigger role. Daily sunscreen should be an absolute nonnegotiable.

But let's go ahead and take the least charitable scenario anyway. Say the commenters are right: Someone spent decades skipping SPF, absolutely roasting in the sun, and personally accumulating the damage now visible on their face. They did, in some meaningful sense, "do it to themselves." When did that become permission to humiliate them for it? The most obvious analogy is pointing out someone's body weight in either extreme direction, a full-on social taboo by now (as it should be). Weight, too, is routinely—and often reductively—understood as the visible consequence of personal choices. Yet we've largely arrived at the understanding that whatever combination of biology, circumstance, and behavior got someone there, their body is not an open invitation for commentary. Why hasn't skin been afforded the same grace? Is there something reassuring about believing that we've made the "right" choices when someone else seemingly hasn't?

Shame is rarely an effective strategy no matter how you serve it up. In fact, according to Dr. Rachel Goldman, New York-based psychologist and author of When Life Happens , it can propel people in the exact opposite direction. "We live in a culture that tells us that if we just make the 'right' choices, use the right products, eat the right way, exercise enough, we can control how we look and how we age," she explains. " We can educate people about the risks of UV exposure, using sunscreen vs. not using sunscreen, without turning it into a judgment about their character." Critically, she adds, health education and shame are two very different things. The cruel remarks are difficult to not internalize, and can feel especially personal when it's about your appearance. "If someone is constantly being told that they look bad, made bad choices, or should be ashamed of their appearance, eventually those external messages can become part of their own internal dialogue," she says.

There is some comfort in this perception of control, too. If someone else's visible aging can be neatly traced back to a series of wrong choices, then perhaps our own can be staved off indefinitely by making all the right ones. The faces in our phone become an FYP of cautionary tales, proof that the rules work, and that we're following them correctly. The rules, too, haven't always been this neatly spelled out. The people getting dragged for visible photodamage in 2026 didn't necessarily spend their entire lives in a culture where daily SPF 50 was a rote part of daily life.

We spent decades actively valorizing tanning—and still do to some extent, as evidenced by the alarming rise of Melanotan —and now we're laughing at the women whose skin bears the evidence of pursuing the beauty standard we handed them. Yesterday's beauty standards have been conveniently recast as today's personal failing. Hindsight makes for one hell of a high horse.

articles.title: Círio 2026: Ação oferece apoio a romeiros na Trasladação em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação será realizada na Praça do Relógio e terá voluntários para oferecer apoio aos participantes da caminhada.
articles.summary: Voluntários oferecem suporte com água, alimentação e saúde para romeiros na Trasladação do Círio 2026, em Belém, e aceitam doações para a iniciativa.
articles.body:
Ação oferece água, alimentação e atendimento a romeiros durante a Trasladação em Belém — Foto: Insituto Somos Um

Uma ação de acolhimento vai oferecer água, alimentação, massagens, curativos e outros atendimentos aos romeiros que participarem da Trasladação, que vai ocorrer no dia 10 de outubro, em Belém .

A iniciativa, promovida pelo Instituto Somos Um, será realizada na Praça do Relógio durante a programação do Círio de Nazaré.

O projeto desenvolve ações sociais, campanhas e projetos voltados à solidariedade e à assistência de pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade. A instituição também incentiva o trabalho voluntário e a participação da comunidade em ações sociais.

A proposta é criar um ponto de apoio para os participantes que enfrentam longas horas de caminhada e esforço físico durante a procissão.

A equipe será formada por voluntários, que estarão no local para prestar assistência aos romeiros e oferecer um espaço de descanso e cuidado ao longo do percurso.

Para realizar a ação, o Instituto Somos Um também está arrecadando doações e buscando pessoas interessadas em atuar como voluntárias.

"A ideia é que cada romeiro que passe pela nossa acolhida encontre um espaço de cuidado, respeito e solidariedade", afirma o instituto.

A população pode contribuir com doações ou participar como voluntária na ação. As informações sobre a campanha e as formas de participação estão disponíveis no Instagram @instituto.somosum.

As doações podem ser encaminhadas pelo e-mail institutosomosumbelem@gmail.com.

articles.title: A casa para uma pessoa só: por que São José dos Campos virou cidade de studio | G1
articles.standfirst: Universitários, jovens profissionais e quem busca autonomia impulsionam a procura por imóveis compactos e transformam o endereço no principal indicador de valorização
articles.summary: Universitários, jovens profissionais e quem busca autonomia impulsionam a procura por imóveis compactos e transformam o endereço no principal indicador de valorização
articles.body:
Morar sozinho deixou de ser uma etapa passageira da vida para virar uma escolha definitiva de milhares de brasileiros. Os domicílios unipessoais cresceram 109,8% desde 2012 e já são 15,6 milhões de pessoas vivendo sozinhas no país — quase um em cada cinco lares, segundo o IBGE, com 45% desse público concentrado no Sudeste. O comportamento tem nome no mercado: 61% da Geração Z pretende comprar imóvel nos próximos anos, e a decisão passa, antes de tudo, por onde o imóvel está e pelo que se resolve a pé a partir dele.

Em São José dos Campos, esse movimento ganha força extra. A cidade é hoje um dos principais polos de tecnologia, inovação e educação do país, com instituições como o ITA e o CTA, além de empresas como a Embraer atraindo, todos os anos, estudantes, pesquisadores e profissionais recém-chegados todos em busca do mesmo tipo de produto: um imóvel bem localizado, funcional e pronto para o dia a dia.

O LIV ONE Residencial Club nasce exatamente para responder a esse público. São 286 studios de 1 dormitório, com metragens entre 30,09 m² e 45,85 m², ao lado do CenterVale Shopping a 2 minutos de carro do shopping, 6 minutos do CTA/ITA e 12 minutos do centro da cidade. Todas as unidades contam com varanda integrada e área de serviço, e algumas tipologias oferecem diferenciais como quintais privativos. Coworking, sala de reunião, sala de podcast, lavanderia compartilhada, academia, lounge, café, piscina e minimercado 24h completam uma rotina pensada para quem trabalha, estuda e circula pela cidade o tempo todo.

O timing também favorece quem decide comprar agora: studios seguem liderando o Índice de Velocidade de Vendas do mercado, segundo o Secovi-SP, e os imóveis de 1 dormitório lideraram a valorização nacional em 2025, com alta de 8,05%. Ou seja, o mesmo produto que resolve a rotina de quem mora sozinho é também, hoje, o que mais valoriza e mais rápido vende.

“Um jeito mais inteligente de viver a cidade” é assim que a Reflora resume o conceito por trás do LIV ONE: unidades desenhadas para autonomia, liberdade e uma experiência urbana completa.

Invista em studios a 2 minutos do CenterVale Shopping.

Localização, mobilidade e um produto alinhado ao perfil de quem mais compra imóvel no Brasil hoje.

Endereço: Rua República do Líbano, 406, São José dos Campos, SP — ao lado do CenterVale Shopping

Unidades: 286 studios de 1 dormitório | Metragens: de 30,09 m² a 45,85 m²

articles.title: Net Turbo inaugura sede em Campinas e abre vagas | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa investiu R$ 9 milhões em espaço com capacidade para 420 colaboradores; há oportunidades para profissionais de tecnologia e telecomunicações
articles.summary: Empresa investiu R$ 9 milhões em espaço com capacidade para 420 colaboradores; há oportunidades para profissionais de tecnologia e telecomunicações
articles.body:
Net Turbo inaugura sede em Campinas e abre vagas – Crédito: Net Turbo.

A Net Turbo Telecom completa 19 anos com uma nova sede em Campinas (SP) e novas oportunidades de trabalho. Localizado na Torre do Castelo, no bairro do Chapadão, o espaço recebeu investimento de cerca de R$ 9 milhões e tem capacidade para até 420 colaboradores.

A nova estrutura foi planejada para acompanhar o crescimento da empresa nos próximos cinco anos, ampliando a capacidade da Net Turbo de estruturar suas equipes e operações. O espaço reúne áreas como novos negócios, marketing, implantação, operações de rede (NOC), segurança digital (SOC) e tecnologia da informação, favorecendo a integração entre diferentes áreas e o desenvolvimento das atividades da empresa.

Segundo a empresa, a nova sede também foi projetada para facilitar a integração entre as equipes e ampliar a estrutura de treinamento e desenvolvimento profissional.

“Chegamos aos 19 anos em um momento importante de crescimento da Net Turbo. A nova sede foi planejada para acompanhar o crescimento da empresa, aproximar nossas equipes e criar um ambiente preparado para os próximos anos”, afirma Eduardo Garcia, fundador e diretor de Novos Negócios da Net Turbo Telecom.

A estrutura conta ainda com mais de 1.500 metros quadrados de área externa, auditório, salas de treinamento, estúdio de podcast e espaços destinados à educação corporativa.

A expansão da empresa também acompanha a abertura de oportunidades profissionais na região. Atualmente, há vagas para a área de tecnologia e TI, comercial, processos, logística e banco de talentos.

A Net Turbo mantém um processo contínuo de recrutamento e afirma ter como foco a contratação de profissionais da Região Metropolitana de Campinas. A empresa também oferece programas de treinamento e plano de carreira.

“Investimos em infraestrutura e também em pessoas. A capacidade da nova sede nos permite ampliar nossas equipes de forma estruturada e criar um ambiente de desenvolvimento profissional”, diz Garcia.

As vagas disponíveis podem ser consultadas no site de oportunidades da Net Turbo .

Net Turbo inaugura sede em Campinas e abre vagas — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação

A nova sede faz parte do plano de expansão da Net Turbo. Para 2026, a empresa prevê investir R$ 12,4 milhões , um aumento de 32% em relação ao valor investido no ano anterior.

A companhia também informa que registrou crescimento de aproximadamente 19% no faturamento em 2025 e projeta alta de 14% em 2026.

A escolha de Campinas para a nova sede está relacionada, segundo a empresa, à localização estratégica da cidade, à proximidade de rodovias e do Aeroporto Internacional de Viracopos e à conexão com municípios da Região Metropolitana de Campinas.

Fundada em 2007, a Net Turbo Telecom é 100% voltada ao mercado corporativo (B2B), com atuação em conectividade, telefonia, segurança, cloud e infraestrutura.

Com cobertura nacional e infraestrutura própria, a empresa conta com atendimento técnico especializado 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana, além de desenvolver projetos sob medida para empresas e ambientes críticos.

A Net Turbo também foi premiada na 4ª edição do Prêmio Abrint/Teleco para Provedores de Internet, da Associação Brasileira de Provedores de Internet e Telecomunicações (Abrint).

articles.title: Com nota 835, Colégio ECCOS conquista selo de excelência em São José | G1
articles.standfirst: Princípios e Valores humanos, educação bilíngue com conexões internacionais e resultados acadêmicos foram fatores determinantes para boa nota da avaliação
articles.summary: Princípios e Valores humanos, educação bilíngue com conexões internacionais e resultados acadêmicos foram fatores determinantes para boa nota da avaliação
articles.body:
O Colégio ECCOS, de São José dos Campos, recebeu a certificação GPTS (Great Place to Study), selo internacional que reconhece instituições de ensino a partir da experiência dos estudantes, familiares e educadores. Com 835 pontos em uma escala de 0 a 1000, a instituição foi reconhecida por oferecer um ambiente seguro, acolhedor e comprometido com o desenvolvimento integral dos estudantes.

O resultado revela como características centrais da proposta do colégio estão conectadas com as demandas educacionais da atualidade. Entre os pontos mais bem avaliados pelas famílias estão o ensino bilíngue e a formação que estimula crianças e adolescentes a interpretar o mundo, conviver com as diferenças, agir com empatia e participar de maneira responsável da sociedade.

O ECCOS é a primeira escola bilíngue de São José dos Campos a receber o selo e uma das duas escolas da cidade certificadas pelo GPTS.

A avaliação ouviu mais de 300 pessoas, entre estudantes, familiares e educadores. O ECCOS ficou acima da média de 726 pontos das instituições pesquisadas e superou os 750 pontos necessários para entrar na Zona de Excelência e conquistar a certificação.

Um dos destaques do Colégio ECCOS é o trabalho realizado nos anos iniciais, no Berçário e Infantil, com uma proposta baseada no afeto, vínculo e produção do conhecimento — Foto: Colégio Eccos

A metodologia do GPTS considera a experiência escolar como um todo. A pesquisa avalia a percepção da comunidade sobre aspectos como qualidade do ensino, segurança, acolhimento, bem-estar, confiança, pertencimento, inclusão, sustentabilidade, inovação e relações entre estudantes, famílias e educadores.

Entre os pontos de destaque do ECCOS estão infraestrutura e segurança, sustentabilidade, equidade, diversidade, senso de pertencimento, respeito, desenvolvimento dos estudantes, propósito, bem-estar e qualidade do corpo docente.

A pesquisa também mostrou que princípios e valores são o principal fator considerado pelas famílias na escolha da escola em todos os segmentos avaliados. A cultura internacional e a formação bilíngue aparecem igualmente entre os aspectos de maior relevância.

112 alunos no Berçário e Educação Infantil

835 pontos no Índice GPTS, que colocou a escola na Zona de Excelência

Para Henry Oliveira, fundador e CEO do Instituto ECCOS de Educação, os resultados refletem uma construção baseada em vínculo, escuta e participação.

“A conquista representa a construção diária de um colégio em que aprender envolve pertencimento e relações significativas. Os alunos se sentem parte da escola, gostam dos professores, criam amizades e percebem que estão aprendendo. As famílias demonstram confiança, transparência e abertura para construir conosco o projeto educacional”, afirma.

A certificação também oferece à escola uma análise de seus pontos fortes e das oportunidades de evolução pedagógica, estrutural e de relacionamento com a comunidade.

“Estamos contentes com o resultado, mas também com o caminho apontado para continuarmos avançando. A proposta vai além da avaliação e oferece uma escuta externa e especializada, que nos ajuda a fortalecer aquilo que fazemos bem, e a cuidar dos aspectos em que ainda podemos evoluir”, diz Oliveira.

No ECCOS, a proposta educacional passa por formar crianças e adolescentes capazes de observar a realidade com atenção, compreender o outro, dialogar com diferentes pontos de vista e assumir responsabilidades diante das questões coletivas.

O conhecimento, nessa perspectiva, não é passivo. Os estudantes são incentivados a perguntar, investigar, argumentar, trabalhar em grupo e transformar o que aprendem em escolhas e iniciativas. Desde cedo, as crianças encontram oportunidades para expressar ideias, escutar, lidar com divergências, participar de decisões e construir soluções coletivas.

Sustentabilidade, diversidade e cidadania global atravessam essa formação e ajudam os estudantes a perceber as conexões entre suas atitudes cotidianas e os grandes desafios da sociedade.

A turma do 9º ano do Colégio ECCOS em Seligenthal, na Alemanha, durante viagem de intercâmbio realizada em julho de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação

O ensino bilíngue começa no Berçário e segue até o Ensino Fundamental 2. A proposta busca ampliar repertórios culturais, apresentar diferentes perspectivas e preparar os estudantes para participar de um mundo cada vez mais conectado.

“A educação bilíngue faz parte do nosso DNA e vai além da língua. Ela envolve a internacionalização da escola e uma ampliação de mundo” , explica Oliveira.

A intenção é formar cidadãos globais que saibam se comunicar em diferentes contextos, mas que também tenham consciência ética, sensibilidade para compreender outras realidades e disposição para contribuir com a sociedade.

Experiências dentro e fora da sala de aula

A prática pedagógica do ECCOS é fundamentada em princípios construtivistas, que colocam o estudante em uma relação ativa com o próprio aprendizado. O professor atua como mediador de um processo que valoriza investigação, questionamento, colaboração, reflexão e produção de conhecimento a partir da experiência.

O nome ECCOS nasceu de uma releitura de quatro pilares da educação (UNESCO, 1996): aprender a Empreender, aprender a Conviver, aprender a Conhecer e aprender a Ser.

Essa formação se estende às atividades extracurriculares. Esportes, música, projetos de leitura e participação em olimpíadas de diferentes áreas criam oportunidades para que os estudantes descubram interesses, enfrentem desafios e desenvolvam criatividade, disciplina, cooperação e autonomia.

A dentista Vanessa Ávila Sarmento Silveira conheceu a escola por intermédio de uma amiga e matriculou a filha, Isabel, no Berçário, quando ela tinha apenas 1 ano. Treze anos depois, ela considera que fez a escolha certa e cita alguns dos motivos.

“Gostei do ECCOS desde a primeira visita. Me chamaram a atenção a organização, o ambiente acolhedor e o método de ensino. Sempre me senti muito segura, e a Isabel sempre vai feliz para a escola, tem um vínculo muito forte, uma sensação de pertencimento. A escola é bastante parceira da família”, afirma.

Para ela, a trajetória da filha no ECCOS trouxe benefícios como a participação em projetos de incentivo à leitura, aprendizado do inglês desde cedo, além de experiências como a participação na OBAFOG (Olimpíada Brasileira de Foguetes), em 2025, na qual Isabel e sua equipe representaram o colégio, no Rio de Janeiro, ganhando medalha.

Isabel Sarmento, aluna do 8º ano do Colégio ECCOS, na OBAFOG 2025, no Rio de Janeiro. — Foto: Divulgação

“Foi uma experiência muito rica, ela era a única menina da equipe, e se hospedou com meninas de outros lugares”, conta Vanessa. “O corpo docente é muito competente. No ensino fundamental, a escola ajuda a desenvolver a autonomia do aluno e a resolver conflitos. Acredito que os alunos estarão bem preparados ao chegarem no ensino médio."

Para a direção do ECCOS, a certificação reconhece a consistência de uma trajetória, mas não representa um ponto de chegada. Os resultados da pesquisa serão utilizados para orientar novas ações e fortalecer a experiência de estudantes, famílias e educadores.

articles.title: A era do home office acabou? O que mostram os dados do IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do IBGE mostram avanço do trabalho presencial nos últimos anos, mas indicam que o país ainda está longe de retornar ao padrão anterior à pandemia.
articles.summary: Dados do IBGE mostram avanço do trabalho presencial nos últimos anos, mas indicam que o país ainda está longe de retornar ao padrão anterior à pandemia.
articles.body:
Desde a pandemia de Covid-19, milhões de brasileiros voltaram a trabalhar dos escritórios, mas até agora o mercado de trabalho não retornou ao mesmo cenário existente antes de 2020.

Dados da PNAD Contínua – Características Adicionais do Mercado de Trabalho 2025, divulgados pelo IBGE nesta quarta-feira (23), mostram que o trabalho realizado em casa perdeu espaço desde o pico registrado após a pandemia, mas permanece maior do que era antes da crise sanitária.

Em 2022, 8,4% dos trabalhadores exerciam suas atividades no próprio domicílio. Em 2025, esse percentual recuou para 7,9%.

No mesmo período, a participação daqueles que trabalham em estabelecimentos físicos cresceu de 57,9% para 60,2%.

Em 2019, por exemplo, apenas 5,8% dos trabalhadores atuavam em casa. Em 2012, o percentual era de 3,6%. Isso mostra que a transformação dos modelos de trabalho começou antes mesmo da Covid-19.

➡️ O avanço do setor de serviços, a digitalização da economia, o crescimento das plataformas digitais e do trabalho autônomo já vinham reduzindo a dependência de um único local fixo de trabalho. A pandemia acelerou esse processo.

Como o IBGE não realizou esse módulo da pesquisa em 2020 e 2021, não é possível medir com precisão o pico dos efeitos das medidas de isolamento. Ainda assim, o salto observado em 2022 mostra a dimensão da mudança.

Muitas empresas descobriram que parte de suas atividades podia ser realizada remotamente. Ao mesmo tempo, milhões de trabalhadores reorganizaram a própria vida levando em conta a possibilidade de trabalhar longe dos escritórios.

Mas esse cenário voltou a mudar nos anos seguintes. Em 2025, 60,2% dos trabalhadores exerciam suas atividades em estabelecimentos do próprio empreendimento. Outros trabalhavam em diferentes locais:

13,8% em locais definidos pelo empregador ou pelo cliente;

8,4% em fazendas, sítios, granjas ou chácaras;

Segundo William Araujo Kratochwill, pesquisador do IBGE, a classificação considera o local onde o trabalhador atua com mais frequência.

📎Isso significa que uma pessoa que trabalha quatro dias por semana em casa e apenas um no escritório pode aparecer na categoria dos que trabalham no domicílio. O inverso também ocorre: trabalhadores híbridos que passam a maior parte da semana na empresa entram no grupo dos que trabalham em estabelecimentos físicos.

Essa observação ajuda a explicar por que o trabalho realizado em casa continua relativamente elevado mesmo após a volta de parte dos profissionais aos escritórios.

Movimento de passageiros na estação Guaianases, na zona leste de São Paulo nesta quarta-feira (5), durante greve na CPTM. — Foto: FÁBIO VIEIRA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Os dados do IBGE acompanham um movimento que já vinha sendo identificado por outras pesquisas sobre o mercado de trabalho.

Um estudo da Robert Half mostrou que profissionais de construção civil e engenharia trabalham, em média, 4,8 dias por semana presencialmente. No setor de serviços, a média é de 3,3 dias.

Outra pesquisa, mencionada em uma reportagem publicada pelo g1 em maio e realizada pela WeWork em parceria com a Offerwise , mostra que 63% dos trabalhadores atuam presencialmente. Entre eles, 79% afirmam que esse modelo é uma determinação da empresa, e não uma escolha pessoal.

Nos últimos anos, as vagas remotas também perderam espaço, enquanto as oportunidades presenciais e híbridas avançaram e passaram a representar a maior parte das ofertas disponíveis no mercado, segundo a Gupy.

Vagas anunciadas com trabalho 100% remoto — Foto: Arte g1

Por que as empresas estão voltando ao presencial?

Outro levantamento da Robert Half sugere que muitas organizações associam a presença física a ganhos de integração, comunicação e fortalecimento da cultura corporativa.

Entre os principais motivos apontados pelos gestores estão:

68% citam o fortalecimento da cultura organizacional;

63% mencionam melhora da comunicação e da colaboração entre equipes;

59% apontam maior integração e supervisão;

50% relacionam o trabalho presencial ao aumento da produtividade.

Mas a volta de parte dos trabalhadores aos escritórios recolocou no centro do debate questões que haviam perdido relevância durante a pandemia, como tempo de deslocamento, gastos com transporte e distância entre casa e trabalho.

A pesquisa da WeWork mostra que 65% dos trabalhadores consideram o trajeto até o escritório a principal desvantagem do trabalho presencial. Mais da metade afirma que passou a gastar mais com transporte e deslocamento.

A gerente de negócios da WeWork Brasil, Beatriz Kawakami, define esse fenômeno como um “custo silencioso”. Ele não aparece diretamente na renda do trabalhador, mas reduz o tempo disponível para a vida pessoal e amplia despesas que haviam diminuído durante o período de maior adesão ao trabalho remoto.

Os impactos, porém, vão além da rotina diária. Durante a pandemia, a possibilidade de trabalhar à distância levou muitas famílias a trocar apartamentos por casas maiores, buscar cidades mais tranquilas, reduzir o custo de vida ou se mudar para mais perto de familiares e áreas verdes.

Essa lógica dependia da manutenção do trabalho remoto como modelo predominante. À medida que mais empresas passaram a exigir a presença dos funcionários alguns dias por semana, a localização voltou a ganhar peso nas decisões de moradia.

Home office trabalho remoto — Foto: Pexels

Um levantamento do Colégio Notarial do Brasil (CNB/SP), divulgado pelo g1 na semana passada, mostrou que a cidade de São Paulo registrou recorde histórico de compra e venda de imóveis em 2025. Foram 90.402 escrituras registradas nos cartórios de notas, volume 49,6% superior ao de 2020.

Ao mesmo tempo, municípios do interior que haviam se beneficiado da expansão do home office passaram a registrar desaceleração nas transações imobiliárias.

Para o vice-presidente do CNB/SP, Andrey Guimarães Duarte, os números indicam que o mercado entrou em uma nova etapa.

“Se fosse simplesmente uma volta ao padrão pré-pandemia, esperaríamos que a capital recuperasse o que perdeu e os destinos do home office retornassem aos níveis anteriores. Não foi exatamente isso que aconteceu”, afirmou.

Apesar dessa mudança, a região Sudeste continua liderando a participação de trabalhadores que atuam dentro de casa, com 8,2%.

Segundo Kratochwill, o resultado pode estar relacionado à forte concentração de empresas e de atividades compatíveis com o trabalho remoto em estados como São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro.

"São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro têm muitas empresas em que o trabalho remoto pode ter uma influência importante devido ao volume de trabalhadores", afirmou.

articles.title: Azul diz que falha em GPS cancelou 80 voos e afeta 8 mil passageiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiros ainda enfrentavam problemas nesta quarta-feira (23), com voos remarcados, falta de assentos e dificuldades para conseguir hospedagem em Campinas (SP).
articles.summary: Passageiros ainda enfrentavam problemas nesta quarta-feira (23), com voos remarcados, falta de assentos e dificuldades para conseguir hospedagem em Campinas (SP).
articles.body:
Avião modelo E195-E2 da Embraer — Foto: Guilherme Ramos

A instabilidade global no sistema de GPS que afetou a operação de aeronaves Embraer E195-E2 impactou 8 mil passageiros da Azul Linhas Aéreas . A companhia informou nesta quarta-feira (23) que mais de 80 voos foram cancelados e outros tiveram atrasos .

Por volta de 8h50, painéis do Aeroporto Internacional de Viracopos, em Campinas (SP), onde fica o principal hub da Azul, indicavam seis voos cancelados . A concessionária que administra o terminal informou que ao menos três estão ligados à falha do GPS.

Com 50 jatos da linha em sua frota, a Azul disse na terça (22) que está adotando medidas operacionais que podem resultar em ajustes na malha e nos horários de alguns voos . Apenas no Aeroporto de Viracopos, 18 voos haviam sido cancelados em decorrência do problema.

O balanço divulgado pela Azul se refere aos impactos registrados na terça. A companhia não informou, até a última atualização dessa reportagem, se há novos cancelamentos ou atrasos relacionados à instabilidade nesta quarta-feira (veja a nota completa abaixo) .

Apesar disso, uma reportagem da EPTV encontrou passageiros em Viracopos que ainda relatavam consequências dos problemas, como voos remarcados, falta de assentos e dificuldades para conseguir hospedagem .

Na manhã desta quarta-feira (23), passageiros ainda enfrentavam os efeitos dos problemas . No Aeroporto Internacional de Viracopos, em Campinas (SP), havia relatos de voos remarcados mais de uma vez, falta de assentos e dificuldades para conseguir hospedagem durante a espera .

A advogada Iandre Lotufo chegou ao aeroporto durante a madrugada depois de ter o voo remarcado. Segundo ela, a companhia aérea encaminhou os passageiros para um hotel, mas, quando chegaram ao local, não havia mais vagas.

"Eles encaminharam a gente para um hotel, que remarcaram nossa passagem para sair aqui de Viracopos, encaminharam a gente para o hotel, só que chegamos no hotel e não tinha mais lugar", relatou.

Sem conseguir se hospedar, o grupo voltou para o aeroporto. Ela contou que chegou ao terminal por volta das 2h e aguardava um novo embarque, previsto para 13h10. "Exaustas. Muito cansativo, porque a gente veio de um voo internacional", afirmou.

O consultor técnico Sérgio Bezan também enfrentava problemas para conseguir viajar. O voo dele estava marcado para 13h de terça-feira, foi cancelado e depois remarcado para 22h30. A viagem foi novamente alterada, desta vez para 8h30 desta quarta.

Ao chegar ao aeroporto, porém, Sérgio descobriu que não havia assento disponível. O consultor detalha que precisava viajar para cumprir um compromisso profissional e que, até o momento da entrevista, não tinha informações sobre quando conseguiria embarcar.

"Não tem informação ainda sobre o que vai fazer, que horas que vai, se vai hoje, se vai sair daqui, se vai estar falando que é para ir para Congonhas. A gente não sabe ainda nada", afirmou.

Os problemas em Campinas começaram ainda na madrugada de terça-feira (22), com uma falha no fornecimento de energia elétrica em parte do terminal . A interrupção começou por volta das 3h10 e afetou sistemas do saguão de check-in.

Durante a manhã, os painéis de informações sobre os voos ficaram inoperantes e os passageiros enfrentaram filas para acessar a área de embarque, que chegaram à porta do terminal. Equipamentos de raio-X também foram afetados, segundo relatos de passageiros.

Às 15h, o saguão ainda funcionava com luzes de emergência, embora os painéis já tivessem sido religados por volta das 9h. A concessionária informou que a pista, o pátio de aeronaves e as vias de acesso não foram afetados.

A Azul informou que 26 voos foram cancelados em razão da queda de energia. Dados do Flightradar24 apontavam, às 16h, 38 voos cancelados e 116 atrasados no aeroporto , embora não houvesse confirmação de que todas as ocorrências estivessem relacionadas ao apagão.

A situação ganhou um novo capítulo no fim da tarde. Uma instabilidade global no sistema de GPS dos aviões Embraer E195-E2 levou a Azul a anunciar ajustes na malha aérea. Entre 17h e 21h, Viracopos registrou 18 cancelamentos — sete voos de partida e 11 de chegada — em razão do problema.

A Azul informou que a instabilidade poderia afetar os 50 jatos E195-E2 que fazem parte de sua frota e orientou passageiros com voos impactados a consultar o status das reservas antes de ir ao aeroporto.

A Embraer afirmou que acompanha a ocorrência e presta suporte técnico às companhias. Segundo a fabricante, embora a instabilidade possa afetar a programação dos voos, não há impacto na segurança de voo.

"A Azul informa que uma instabilidade global no sistema de GPS impactou a operação de aeronaves Embraer E2-195 e levou ao cancelamento de mais de 80 voos ao longo do dia de ontem. Em consequência dos cancelamentos, alguns voos também sofreram atrasos, com impacto para mais de 8 mil Clientes.

A Azul reforça que os Clientes afetados estão recebendo a assistência prevista na Resolução 400 da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) e que as medidas operacionais foram adotadas com foco na segurança, valor primordial para a Companhia".

Em comunicado, a Embraer informou que foi notificada sobre relatos de instabilidade no sistema GPS e que acompanha a situação de perto junto aos operadores e ao fabricante do equipamento.

"A empresa está fornecendo suporte técnico aos clientes e conduzindo as ações necessárias para a resolução da questão. Embora a ocorrência possa afetar a programação operacional de companhias aéreas, não há impacto na segurança de voo".

A fabricante destaca ainda que a frota de aeronaves E2 dispõe de sistemas e procedimentos de navegação "para operar mesmo em condições de instabilidade no sistema GPS, capazes de garantir uma operação segura em conformidade com os requisitos aplicáveis das autoridades de aviação civil.”

articles.title: In 2005, a California engineer used Google Earth to challenge a logging plan above Los Gatos Creek; community pressure later helped spare 1,000 acres of redwood watershed
articles.summary: US News: In 2005, residents of the Santa Cruz Mountains utilized Google Earth to successfully combat a logging plan proposed by San Jose Water Company, saving 1,000 acres of redwood watershed. Discover the impact of technology in environmental activism and the community's journey against corporate development.
articles.body: Residents who oppose corporate development plans frequently find it difficult to understand complicated legal notifications and technical maps that unexpectedly arrive in the mail. When a group of landowners in the Santa Cruz Mountains of California got an official notification in 2005 detailing a proposal to chop a sizable area of forest above their homes, they found themselves in precisely that predicament. What transpired became one of the first instances of ordinary people using digital mapping technology to oppose a powerful organisation and alter the course of a local environmental battle.The warning was from the San Jose Water Company, a company that owns about 6,000 acres in the Los Gatos Creek watershed, a source of drinking water for more than 100,000 people in Silicon Valley. The company submitted a plan in August 2005 to cut about 1,000 acres of forest including coast redwoods and Douglas fir along a six-mile section of canyon, and copies of a black and white map explaining the plan were mailed to neighbouring people. For many, the document was almost impossible to comprehend as it gave little differentiation between roads, contour lines and the real borders of the proposed logging zone.Making sense of the mapOne of the residents to get the warning was engineer Rebecca Moore, who was working on a mapping tool within Google that would become known as Google Earth Outreach. Instead of relying on the confused paper map, Moore set out to make her own map using satellite imagery and aerial pictures of the entire watershed. She helped create a neighbourhood group, Neighbours Against Irresponsible Logging, and utilised the new Google Earth software to map the proposed logging area much more accurately than the utility’s initial document had done.Moore’s computer map did more than map out boundaries. She layered in geo-located photographs of old-growth redwoods that stood in the way of the plan, added sightings of local wildlife such as ospreys and beavers, and imported data that showed that endangered red-legged frogs lived in the canyon, directly contradicting the company’s claim that no protected species were present. She also teamed with a colleague to build a three-dimensional flypast of a simulated helicopter carrying cut redwood trunks on a flight path over nearby schools and residences.The evidence offeredMoore’s presentation of her flypast at the group’s inaugural community gathering had an instant impact. Residents who had failed to interpret a flat printed map could suddenly see, in three dimensions, how narrow mountain roads laced with more than 30 blind curves would convey a dozen 90,000-pound logging trucks each day past pathways frequented by children heading to school. The presentation gave the community a common and correct picture of exactly what the logging plan would do for their neighbourhood, which the initial notification had not provided.Separately, opponents of the plan objected to the size of the company’s assets. Residents said their own aerial surveys showed the company’s actual holdings exceeded a ceiling set by California law on the amount of commercially harvestable forest a single owner could hold and still qualify for the kind of open-ended logging permit the water company wanted. The issue was sent to California’s forestry regulator, which has standards for assessing proposals like these established by the CAL FIRE Board of Forestry and Fire Protection.A campaign that made a differenceEventually community pressure and more regulatory issues pushed a turning point. By December 2007, almost two years after the original notice was mailed, the water company had withdrawn its logging proposal, and California’s forestry department had found the plan invalid under the laws that governed it. The result, for the redwood watershed above Los Gatos, was that some 1,000 acres of forest were saved from the large-scale cutting which the original plan had called for.The episode also had repercussions well beyond a small canyon in California. Moore’s success in using Google Earth to expose the difference between a company’s official map and the actual size of its plans became one of the origin stories for Google Earth Outreach, a programme designed specifically to help environmental and community groups use mapping technology in their own campaigns. Moore has said the fight above Los Gatos Creek influenced her later work creating tools to detect deforestation and environmental change across continents.Today, San Jose Water owns and manages thousands of acres in the same watershed and describes its approach to the property in terms of long-term stewardship rather than massive-scale timber harvesting. The 2005 controversy is one of the most startling early examples of how accessible digital mapping can shift the power from major institutions to locals, changing what may have been an intractable bureaucratic war into a contest that ordinary people could see clearly enough to win.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Venezuela’s unelected leader Delcy Rodríguez seeks lost legitimacy. Will she get it?
articles.summary: When she addresses the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, Delcy Rodríguez will stand just a 20-minute cab ride from where her deposed predecessor Nicolás Maduro languishes in pre-trial detention.
articles.body: When she addresses the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, Delcy Rodríguez will stand just a 20-minute cab ride from where her deposed predecessor Nicolás Maduro languishes in pre-trial detention. Looking at the agenda she has followed during her trip to New York, Rodríguez appears to have allowed enough time ahead of her address to try to bring her country out of the isolation it has faced since 2018, when Maduro delivered the last speech at that forum by a Venezuelan head of state. After landing in the United States on Monday, Rodríguez said she had arrived “with the firmness and hope of a people that believes in dialogue and unity among nations.” The same day, she met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres; Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) President Ilan Goldfajn; World Bank Group President Ajay Banga; and International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva. It is unclear what benefits these meetings might bring Rodríguez, still bedeviled by questions of legitimacy because she was not elected to the position she holds. But time’s passage is working in her favor. While Donald Trump’s presidency ends in January 2029, there is still no date for Venezuela’s next presidential election. If she withstands pressure from the current US administration, which has many irons in the diplomatic fire, the Chavismo movement of which she is the current torch-bearer will be better positioned to face the future. It still controls the state apparatus, and there are no signs of that changing any time soon. Rodríguez met with Trump on Tuesday on the sidelines of the General Assembly, during which the leaders “discussed strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security,” Rodríguez said in a post on X, alongside a photo of the two. For now, Rodríguez has in Trump her main and unexpected backer. Gone are the days when, as Maduro’s vice president in September 2019, she used a UN General Assembly address to accuse Washington of imposing “a new form of state terrorism without using bombs, but rather through banks and insurance companies.” She was referring at the time to US sanctions that prevented the South American country from selling its oil through the global financial system. The acting president’s trip is also the next step in the process of relaunching diplomatic relations following Maduro’s capture by elite American Delta Force soldiers on January 3. Since then, Venezuela has reactivated consular relations with Chile, Ecuador, Peru, the Dominican Republic and Israel, and has received visits from two Latin American presidents: Colombia’s Gustavo Petro before he left the Nariño Palace and, more recently, Paraguay’s head of state, Santiago Peña. Trump has presented Venezuela as his great foreign-policy victory, and repeatedly emphasizes how he is overseeing the country after winning what he now describes as a war. The latest demonstration came Tuesday in his speech before the delegations attending the General Assembly. “To the victor belong the spoils,” he said, referring to the agreement signed by the Pentagon with private energy company Nabep to gain access to 65 billion barrels of oil from Venezuelan reserves. This display of dominance contrasts with the stalemate in the war with Iran and the inability to successfully mediate a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, all amid the impact of rising fuel prices in the US and a decline in his popularity five weeks before midterm elections. Rodríguez appears to be taking advantage of this situation to present herself as a reliable partner, willing to leave behind the image projected by Maduro’s government and to bolster the political survival of the Chavismo project at the expense of opposition leader María Corina Machado, who is currently stranded outside Venezuela. According to her spokesman, Machado made three attempts to return to Venezuela while Rodríguez was away, but was refused entry. But is Washington’s support enough to overlook the fact that Rodríguez does not hold the presidency as the result of free elections? For Brazil’s president, it is not. Earlier this week, in an interview with CNN, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was highly critical of the relationship Washington and Caracas have been forging in recent months. In his view, Trump has demonstrated that he plays a “very dominant role” over the South American country, while stating that “Venezuela’s sovereignty is over.” During the interview, the Brazilian president said that, if he were in Rodríguez’s position, he would call national elections so that Venezuelans could decide the political direction of their country. In his address to the UN plenary, he once again invoked that same combative discourse and defense of the principle of sovereignty that he displayed in the interview, contrasting with the silence of the other countries in the region over the absence of a firm date for presidential elections in Venezuela. Rodríguez will have her turn on Wednesday, and there is considerable anticipation surrounding her speech at a forum where global concerns are routinely aired. For many years, Chavismo relied on the condemnation of imperialism to construct its political identity, and consistently invoked it on this stage. Now, Washington’s imperial ambitions have been deployed much more forcefully through the revival of the Monroe Doctrine – and a fierce initiative to deport as many migrants as possible from US territory, which has particularly affected the Venezuelan community. Before January 3, Chavismo would have railed forcefully against these policies. For Delcy Rodríguez, this is no longer the case. CORRECTION: This story has been updated to correct the date when Rodriguez is speaking at the UN General Assembly.

articles.title: Gunmen attack South Africa house party, killing 11, including woman believed to be pregnant
articles.summary: Eleven people, including a woman believed to be pregnant, were killed when gunmen opened fire at a house south of the South African city of Durban, police said Wednesday.
articles.body: Eleven people, including a woman believed to be pregnant, were killed when gunmen opened fire at a house south of the South African city of Durban, police said Wednesday. Three gunmen entered the house in the Ziko area of KwaMakhutha on Tuesday night and shot the group as they were having a party, according to police. Ten people died at the scene and another died after being taken to hospital. Three others were wounded. Police have launched a manhunt for the attackers. Acting National Police Commissioner Puleng Dimpane said investigators were following a “promising lead.” The motive is not yet known. Police said some of the victims had previously come to the attention of Crime Intelligence over alleged illegal activities, but did not give further details. They said a feud between rival groups could not be ruled out. South Africa has seen several other deadly mass shootings in recent years. In June, 12 people were killed in an informal settlement in a Johannesburg suburb. Six months earlier, nine people were killed when gunmen opened fire at a tavern outside Johannesburg. In another attack, in KwaZulu-Natal in 2023, 10 members of one family, including a 13-year-old boy, were shot dead at their home. The shootings come amid a much wider problem with violent crime. The latest official police figures show that an average of 58 people were murdered each day in South Africa between January and March. The violence has also left women particularly fearful. In recent weeks, the discovery of the bodies of 10 women in parts of Johannesburg, the country’s largest city, has caused widespread alarm. Several of the bodies were found near roads or in open areas, and police are investigating whether some of the deaths are connected. Beyond these killings, South Africa is battling powerful criminal networks involved in drugs, extortion, illegal mining and gang violence. The 2025 Africa Organized Crime Index says cocaine from South America passes through the country on its way to other parts of the world. Organized crime has also become an issue within the country’s police leadership. Police minister Senzo Mchunu was placed on leave last year after accusations that he had links to a criminal syndicate and interfered with police investigations. He has denied the allegations. President Cyril Ramaphosa said in February that organized crime was “the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development.” Ramaphosa announced that soldiers would be deployed to support police in tackling gang violence, as the government steps up its fight against criminal syndicates.

articles.title: Spain allows U.S. extradition case against pro-Palestinian donor to proceed
articles.summary: Spain allowed a U.S. extradition request for pro-Palestinian donor James Cox Chambers to ‌proceed to court, despite protests from the government.
articles.body: Spain on Tuesday allowed a U.S. extradition request for pro-Palestinian donor James Cox Chambers to ‌proceed to court, despite protests from the government’s left-wing coalition partners who argue the case is politically motivated. The case is politically sensitive for Spain’s Socialist-led government, whose pro-Palestinian stance has drawn rebuke from the Trump administration and contributed to wider ​tensions with Washington. Chambers, 41, an American multimillionaire media heir known as Fergie, was arrested at the ​request of US authorities on July 10 while on holiday in Ibiza. He ⁠is currently in pre-trial detention in Madrid. A self-described anti-imperialist and communist, Chambers has called in interviews and ​on social media for the destruction of the United States. He received $250 million after divesting from his ​family’s media conglomerate, Cox Enterprises, in 2023, his spokesperson said. Chambers has donated over $1 million to humanitarian causes in Gaza and paid legal fees for some members of the activist group Palestine Action, according to his legal team. The group was designated ​as a terrorist organization by the U.S. and U.K. for its actions which include targeting Israel-linked defense companies by blocking ​entrances and spraying paint. The United States has not publicly detailed the charges against Chambers. His legal team says they include ‌money ⁠laundering and conspiracy to commit disorderly conduct. The Department of Justice declined to comment on the charges. The case has attracted widespread attention from pro-Palestinian figures, with 150 prominent activists and celebrities, including Richard Gere, Greta Thunberg and Fatima Bhutto, signing a letter urging Spain not to move forward with the extradition proceedings. Both Chambers’ ​lawyers and Sumar, the ​Socialists’ junior coalition partner, ⁠say that the lack of publicly available evidence suggests he is being targeted for his political views. Under Spanish law, extradition cannot proceed if a request ​is found to be politically motivated. “This extradition would set an alarming precedent in ​Europe if ⁠Spain permits the Trump administration to criminalise humanitarian aid vital to the Palestinian people,” said Chambers’ lawyer Baltasar Garzon, who has filed an application for asylum for Chambers in Spain. Government spokesperson Elma Saiz said the decision to ⁠advance ​the case was “purely procedural”, adding that the cabinet would make ​the final determination after the court process concludes. A date for the hearing would be set in the coming weeks, a court spokesperson ​said.

articles.title: This year’s El Nino-driven heat could cause nearly half a million more deaths, group says
articles.summary: This year’s powerful El Nino, along with severe droughts, wildfires and shrinking water supplies, could lead to nearly half a million more deaths worldwide, according to a research report.
articles.body: BENGALURU, India — This year’s powerful El Nino and the record global heat it’s driving, along with severe droughts, wildfires and shrinking water supplies, could lead to nearly half a million more deaths worldwide by the end of February, according to a research report released Wednesday. The grim warning by the University of Chicago-based Climate Impact Lab says that as many as 451,000 more heat-related deaths between June and the end of February could be attributed to El Nino, compared with heat deaths expected in a typical year. The heaviest toll, the group says, is expected in poorer countries, already struggling with food insecurity and high energy costs, partly due to climate change and the fallout of the war in Iran. Michael Greenstone, a co-founder of the group and the study’s co-author, said the heat danger will likely persist beyond February — even though this El Nino is expected to end by then. The fallout of the weather phenomenon could be felt well into next summer, he added. The research, he said, shows that heat is most dangerous in places that are already hot and relatively poor. “If you’re already in a hot place, the extra couple of degrees are going to be much more dangerous,” he said. Wealthier places, he added, generally have greater access to air conditioning, reliable water supplies and functioning health systems. The study combined seasonal temperature forecasts with localized estimates of how high temperatures affect mortality across more than 24,000 regions worldwide. Researchers estimated the additional heat-related deaths by comparing deaths expected under El Nino-driven high temperatures with deaths expected if temperatures remained similar to what they have been in the last three decades. The projected fatalities are for the entire El Nino period, from June 2026 until the end of February 2027. The report says the Global South will see more heat-related deaths The study by Greenstone and his colleagues also warns that the Global South — a term that isn’t geographical but a reference to developing countries in general — will bear the heaviest burden of the excessive heat. The researchers behind the report found that the Sahel region in Africa — countries along the semiarid southern fringe of the Sahara Desert — is expected to be the hardest-hit, with about 66,800 additional deaths caused by El Nino-driven heat. Other major hot spots include South and Southeast Asia and parts of Latin America, according to the report. The researchers project about 19,400 additional heat-related deaths across the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia, as well as 19,300 in Indonesia, 15,800 in India and 13,300 in Brazil. Heat warnings and cooling centers could prevent thousands of deaths With such staggering numbers, there are recommended measures that governments can take, the report says. They include heat-warning systems, cooling centers, hydration stations, protections for outdoor workers, expanded hospital capacity and targeted outreach to elderly people and other vulnerable groups. The authors also call for what they describe as anticipatory financing, so governments can move resources before dangerous heat peaks. Abhiyant Tiwari, a heat expert at NRDC India who was not involved in the study, said the report’s projections should serve as a call to action rather than be another reason for alarm. But while it’s one thing to have well thought-out plans — as India does — implementing these plans and raising needed funds remains a challenge, he said. “The real measure of our preparedness is not how many heat warnings we issue, but how effectively we protect people and reduce preventable deaths,” Tiwari added. Climate change is amplifying El Nino’s record heat El Nino is a natural climate pattern, but this year’s unusually strong event is occurring on a planet already warmed by human-caused climate change, increasing the risks from extreme heat. The Climate Impact Lab said global land temperatures during this El Nino could be higher by about 1.2 Celsius (2.1 Fahrenheit), producing 44% more extremely hot days than in a typical year. The report said those temperature increases may mirror conditions that climate change could make common some 20 years from now. That’s why this El Nino could offer a preview of what’s ahead as the planet continues to warm, the report said. It’s also an opportunity for decision-makers “to see exactly where emergency actions can be taken now to save tens of thousands of lives,” the authors say.

articles.title: William and Catherine join Tom Cruise at Digger premiere
articles.summary: William and Catherine renew their friendship with the Hollywood star at the  premiere for his film Digger.
articles.body:
The Prince and Princess of Wales renewed their friendship with Tom Cruise at the premiere of the Hollywood star's latest film in London on Tuesday.

Cruise took the hand of Catherine, Princess of Wales, as they talked and laughed on a black carpet - instead of the traditional red - before the royal gala screening of Digger in Leicester Square.

Cruise has known the prince and princess for a number of years and also met William's mother, Princess Diana, and attended her funeral in 1997.

Catherine wore a pair of Diana's pearl drop earrings to the premiere on Tuesday, as well as the late Queen Mother's amethyst sautoir necklace.

Cruise complimented Prince William on his "great jacket", referring to the prince's black velvet jacket.

Catherine wore a purple, floor-length Jenny Packham dress.

David Beckham was among the other big names at the premiere, along with his sons Cruz and Romeo.

Digger sees Cruise transformed into a grey-haired oil baron who has to clean up his environmental mess, and is directed by Oscar winner Alejandro González Iñárritu.

Full reviews have not yet been published, but critics' reactions on social media have been mixed.

IndieWire's Anne Thompson described it as "a brave and gorgeous art film that will not score with mainstream audiences but will play best for the Academy" - referring to the Oscars voters.

But Awards Radar editor Joey Magidson said it is "a mess" and "wasn't enjoyable".

The film will be released in the UK and US on 2 October.

articles.title: Medieval ring found by Suffolk detectorists fails to sell
articles.summary: Two detectorists hoped the 14th Century ring would sell for between £25,000 and £30,000.
articles.body:
A medieval gold ring unearthed by two metal detectorists has failed to sell at auction.

The 14th Century gold seal ring of Matilda was listed for auction by Noonans Mayfair as part of a sale of jewellery, watches, silver and objects of vertu on Tuesday.

It was discovered in a ploughed field near Stoke Ash in Suffolk, in April 2024, by friends Aaron Pizzey, 30, and James Race, 39.

The men said they were disappointed the ring failed to meet its reserve bid of £8,500, but they would attempt to auction it again in the future.

The ring had been estimated to fetch between £10,000 and £12,000, but the men hoped it would auction for even more, somewhere between £25,000 and £30,000.

Noonans said it had a carnelian intaglio engraved with the image of a griffin and its inscription was believed to give a clue to its original owner.

The words "GRIFFVnMATILIELEMATILIOVR" are inscribed on the ring and may be translated as 'griffin Matilda the maternal countess', which could suggest the ring belonged to Matilda of Lancaster, who became Countess of Ulster.

In 1347-8 she became a canoness of the Augustinian Campsey Priory, near Wickham Market - about 20 miles from where the ring was found.

Pizzey explained that the ring had taken a long time to come to auction due to it having to go through a treasure process and he said it was a "shame" it had not sold.

He had hoped to use the money toward upgrading his metal detector and potentially toward a house renovation.

"It's a bit of a niche item because the band is broken," he told BBC Radio Suffolk's Wayne Bavin.

"We decided to leave it as found so that the person who bought it can make their mind up if they want to leave it as is or have it repaired professionally to be worn again."

Race had wanted to use the money for wedding costs and paying off a mortgage.

"There's another auction, I think in two months," he said.

"My first ring that I went and put through Noonans, they did a very good job on that ring and for this lot.

"With my previous one a medieval gold Stuart ring with a sapphire gem, that didn't go the first time either, so it's not uncommon because it's happened twice now."

The men also managed to find a hoard of 60 gold Roman coins in February in Eye and were similarly going through the treasure process again before hoping to auction them.

articles.title: Farmers' race for £233m funding like 'scramble for Oasis tickets'
articles.summary: Farmers fear they may not be able to carry out environmental work because they lost out on funding.
articles.body:
Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours.

Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets.

The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST.

The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027.

The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket.

It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget".

NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise. Its closure in less than six hours shows the scale of demand there is from farmers to deliver for the environment and to invest in farm resilience.

"The current cashflow pressures facing farmers and growers only exacerbates that demand as they look for certainty and clarity for the year ahead."

Vicki Hird, agriculture lead at the Wildlife Trusts said "the scramble for green farming schemes was worse than the dash for Oasis tickets".

She added: "The budget has been inadequate for far too long and the Treasury must recognise this and allocate far greater funds to ensure climate resilience in farming in the next budget."

The SFI scheme is vital for many farmers who have turned large swathes of their land over to nature-friendly schemes, such as planting hedges, creating wildflower margins and protecting the soil.

When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high.

The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements.

Cambridgeshire arable farmer Martin Lines, who leads the NFFN, said: "This entire SFI system, with windows opening and closing within a few hours, isn't fit for purpose.

"We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone."

He pointed out that after years of extreme weather, many farmers were relying on the funding to help adapt their farms to climate change and become more resilient.

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it would provide further information on future opportunities for funding applications in 2027 "soon".

A Defra spokesperson said: "This year we ensured small farms and those new to SFI were prioritised - with an exclusive first window in the summer.

"In anticipation of high demand in the second window, ministers decided to allocate an additional £20m to the fund, on top the £50m announced by the prime minister in August, so that we could fund as many agreements as possible."

Farming Minister Stephen Morgan added that the SFI had been designed to be simpler to apply for and that farmers had "responded in force".

"This is a scheme that works for farmers, backs food production, and delivers practical, sustainable land management, supporting the aims of our farming roadmap, our long-term plan for English farming," he said.

articles.title: The DSA’s dangerous fine print. They're coming for millionaires (and you)
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed's tax proposals target capital gains, inheritances and trusts starting at $1 million, reaching well beyond just billionaires.
articles.body: "Tax the billionaires." You think this is what you hear from Democratic Social Candidates, but it might be time you start reading their websites and examining their policies. While these are easy campaign slogans, there is a far more dangerous tax villain lurking in the alleyways. It’s called taxing middle America and the legacy they want to leave their kids when they don’t even know it. Some of the tax proposals being advanced by democratic socialists don't stop with Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos. They start with the average family living on Main Street America. LET SOCIALISTS ROB FROM THE RICH 100% AND YOU STILL WON’T BE ABLE TO PAY THE BILLS Policies start hitting at $1 million. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's tax platform is a fascinating example. He supports taxing capital gains above $1 million as ordinary income. He wants to eliminate stepped-up basis. This means your kids pay taxes on that appreciated Nvidia or Apple you own, your real estate that has gone up in value and even those baseball cards you’ve been storing in the attic. PROGRESSIVES WANT TO TAX BILLIONAIRES FIRST, AND YOU'RE NEXT ON THE LIST He supports taxing inheritances greater than $1 million as ordinary income. Did you realize that life insurance you own is INCLUDED in your estate? So even if you aren’t considered wealthy, those life insurance proceeds may be income tax-free, but they won’t escape estate taxes under Sayed’s policies unless you put more thought into your plan. He wants higher marginal income-tax rates above $1 million. EL-SAYED ADMITS FREE HEALTHCARE MEANS PAYING 'A LITTLE BIT MORE IN TAXES' REGARDLESS OF INCOME He supports a progressive tax on wealth held in trusts. Then there's a separate wealth tax on billionaires. Duh? Wait until you see what happens on the ballot in California when my prediction is that the billionaires tax passes. And he wants to eliminate the Social Security payroll-tax cap. That's quite a list. THE MILLION-DOLLAR TRAP Here's what Americans need to understand. Income and wealth aren't the same thing. Someone who earns $1 million every year is doing extremely well. THE CURE FOR SOCIALISM IS GIVING MORE AMERICANS A STAKE IN CAPITALISM But, someone who realizes a $1 million capital gain after building a business for 30 years is an entirely different financial situation. You are talking about the owner that’s spent a lifetime running the local convenience store, the bridal shop in your town, and even the people who own a franchise in every strip mall in America. Imagine your local plumber, electrician, or HVAC owner. They start with one truck. Thirty years later, they have 10 trucks, 20 employees and finally sell the company. That business may represent most or all of their retirement savings. Under El-Sayed's proposal, capital gains above $1 million would be taxed at ordinary-income rates rather than today's preferential long-term capital-gains rates. That's not taxing some imaginary billionaire sitting on a yacht. That's taxing the American Dream when somebody finally cashes it in. THEN TAX THE INHERITANCE Now suppose our plumber dies and leaves assets to his children. El-Sayed proposes eliminating stepped-up basis and taxing inheritances above $1 million as ordinary income. For perspective, the federal estate-tax exclusion in 2026 is $15 million per individual. That's an enormous difference in where tax policy begins touching accumulated family wealth. And $1 million isn't what it used to be. A house, retirement accounts and a small business can push a family across that line without anyone remotely resembling a billionaire. This doesn’t even include the life insurance I mentioned. THEN HIT THE PAYCHECK Social Security currently taxes employee wages at 6.2%, matched by another 6.2% from employers, up to $184,500 in 2026. El-Sayed wants to eliminate that ceiling. Take somebody earning $1 million. At today's rates, removing the cap entirely would produce roughly another $50,000 of employee Social Security tax and another $50,000 from the employer, before considering how future benefits would be treated. Call that whatever you want. It's a major tax increase on labor and a backhanded tax on corporate America. TAX THE TRUST TOO Then there's wealth held in trusts. Trusts aren't exclusively toys for billionaires. Families use trusts for estate planning, business succession, children, grandchildren and asset management. El-Sayed specifically proposes a progressive tax on wealth held by trusts. Think about the philosophy underneath all these proposals. Earn substantial money? Tax more of it. Sell the asset you built? Potentially tax more of the gain. Pass wealth to your children? Tax the inheritance and eliminate stepped-up basis. Put assets in a trust? Tax the wealth there. Earn above the Social Security ceiling? Remove the ceiling. Become a billionaire? Add another wealth tax. WHEN IS ENOUGH, ENOUGH? Supporters argue these policies would make wealthy Americans contribute more while El-Sayed's proposed federal tax exemption on the first $50,000 of income would help working households. We know half the country doesn’t pay federal tax anyway. That's an important part of his proposal. But Americans should also understand the other side of the equation. Taxes change incentives. They affect investing. Why should I take risk with no reward? They affect business sales. Why sell my business when I will lose half of what I get? They affect succession planning. Why work a lifetime to set your family up when the Government takes it away? They ultimately affect how much entrepreneurs ultimately keep after taking enormous risks. And they affect whether accumulated family wealth survives from one generation to the next. The Democratic Socialists of America's national program explicitly calls for "aggressive wealth taxes" on wealthy individuals and corporations. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION El-Sayed's proposals are just one example that shows what that philosophy can look like when somebody starts putting actual policies on paper. Problem is most people will hear the headlines and won’t read the fine print. And that's why the most important number in his tax plan is NOT $1 billion. IT IS $1 million. Because once the conversation moves from taxing billionaires to taxing million-dollar gains, million-dollar inheritances, high incomes, we're no longer talking exclusively about America's 800 or so billionaires.
